External-kernel registry — the RUN-TIME side of the external-kernel mechanism.

Kernels are registered by NAME in this process-global registry and resolved at
run time by the numpy backend when it executes an `external_call` op. The
mechanism is kernel-agnostic: the callable contract is plain numpy arrays in,
plain numpy arrays (or a `core.Tensor` / tuple of them) out — a triton
kernel written against this interface (in a DIFFERENT repo) will plug in via
the same `register_external_kernel` call. The `device_resident=True`
opt-in swaps host numpy arrays for device `core.Tensor` s (see that mode's
bullet below): operands export zero-copy via DLPack
(`torch.from_dlpack(tensor)`) and a returned `torch.Tensor` is imported
back zero-copy — the Triton round trip.

The registry is PER-BACKEND: each name maps to a dict of backend slots
(`{backend_or_None: (callable, device_resident)}`), where `None` is the
DEFAULT slot.
Resolution at dispatch time is `get_external_kernel_entry(name, backend)`
(mode-aware: it also reports the slot's device-resident flag) — the exact
backend slot first, then the default slot, then `None`. A kernel registered
with the plain two-argument form lives in the default slot and is used by
every backend. A portable decomposition (a `@evoxc.defn` graph function,
registered via `register_portable`) is the OPTIONAL graph-side
implementation: `vmap`/`grad` fall back to inlining it (pre-registered
fallback rules under `external:<name>`) when no explicit transform rules
exist. `register_external_kernel` returns an `ExternalKernel` handle
offering decorator-style registration of backend impls, the portable, the
transform rules, and the declarative batched-variant sugar
(`ExternalKernel.batch_invariant` / `ExternalKernel.batch_variant`
— see the derived-name convention below).

Binding rules (see `evoxc/CONTEXT.md`, "External kernels"):

- Callable signature: `fn(*np_arrays) -> ndarray | Tensor | tuple/list of
  them`. The number/dtype/shape of the returned arrays must match the specs
  declared by the `external_call` op that invoked the kernel — the numpy
  backend validates count/dtype/shape at run time (`BackendError` /
  `ShapeError` — never a silent coercion).
- DEVICE-RESIDENT mode (explicit opt-in, no magic): `device_resident=True`
  registers a kernel that receives and returns DEVICE tensors — never host
  numpy arrays. It REQUIRES an explicit per-backend slot (`backend` must be
  a string; `device_resident=True` with `backend=None` raises
  `TypeError` — a device kernel in the default slot would receive host
  numpy arrays from the numpy backend). Any non-None backend string is
  accepted as today (backend-neutral); in v1 only the iree adapter consumes
  the flag: it passes the boundary's device-resident `core.Tensor`
  operands DIRECTLY to the kernel (never `.numpy()`-staged) and validates
  device-payload results METADATA-ONLY (count/dtype/shape — never a host
  copy). Host-mode kernels (the default, and every pre-existing
  registration) keep the exact numpy-in/numpy-out contract.

ZERO-COPY TRITON/TORCH ROUND TRIP (iree v1). Each operand is a
  `core.Tensor` whose `.data` is the public
  `evoxc.backends.adapters.iree.IreeDevicePayload` on the run's device; the
  tensor itself is a DLPack EXPORTER (`core.Tensor.__dlpack__` /
  `__dlpack_device__` delegate to the payload), so a kernel imports it with
  `torch.from_dlpack(tensor)` (or any other DLPack consumer) and shares the
  HAL buffer — no host copy in either direction. The kernel may RETURN a
  `torch.Tensor`: the iree adapter imports it through
  `HalDevice.from_dlpack_capsule` as a device payload on the run's device
  (its `__dlpack_device__` must match the executable's device — mismatch
  raises an explicit `BackendError`), so a Triton launch re-enters the graph
  zero-copy. Four rules the kernel author owns:

def triton_kernel(x):                  # device tensors in, torch out
          t = torch.from_dlpack(x)           # zero-copy import of the operand
          out = launch_my_triton_kernel(t)   # a torch.Tensor
          torch.cuda.synchronize()           # (1) see below
          return out                         # (2) zero-copy import back

(1) SYNCHRONIZATION: the adapter adds NO fence around the import or the
  export. iree's HIP/CUDA HAL runs on its OWN stream, so a result still
  pending on torch's stream must be synchronized (`torch.cuda.synchronize()`
  / stream ordering) before returning — otherwise the next segment may read
  in-flight memory. The export direction is safe as-is: iree's `run` blocks
  on its device queue before results are handed to you.
  (2) The returned tensor's memory is kept alive by the imported HAL buffer
  (verified: it survives the producer object), and it must live on the
  executable's device.
  (3) No dtype adaption: the buffer's own element type is what crosses the
  boundary (a dtype the HAL cannot express natively refuses the export).
  (4) `device_resident` kernels are PURE and the registry is process-global
  and never serialized — re-register in every process that runs the graph.
- Registration is process-global and REPLACES any previous registration in
  the same backend slot (last registration wins — documented overwrite
  semantics; this makes hot-reloading kernels and adapter re-registration
  safe). The device-resident mode is stored per slot and is replaced along
  with the callable on re-registration.
- DERIVED (batched-variant) names: kernels registered through
  `ExternalKernel.batch_variant` live under the deterministic derived
  name `f"{name}{_EVOXC_BATCH_SUFFIX}"` — public-by-convention. The suffix is
  RESERVED: user-facing registrations (`register_external_kernel`,
  `register_portable`) reject names containing it; internal derived
  registrations go through the module-private `_register_external_kernel_derived`
  path, and `unregister_external_kernel` cleans up a name's derived
  slots/portable along with its own.
- The registry is NOT serialized: graph artifacts carry only the kernel name;
  any process that runs a graph must re-register its kernels first
  (`BackendError` naming the kernel otherwise).
- Errors are loud: registering a non-callable / bad name / bad backend /
  non-bool `device_resident` raises `TypeError`; unregistering a name
  that was never registered (neither kernel slots nor a portable) raises
  `KeyError`; resolving an unknown name returns `None` (the numpy
  backend turns that into `BackendError`).

## Symbols

- [`ExternalKernel`](/api/evoxc/external/externalkernel/) — Handle returned by `register_external_kernel` — the registration surface for one external kernel.
- [`get_external_kernel`](/api/evoxc/external/get-external-kernel/) — The callable for `name` at `backend` (`None` if unknown).
- [`get_external_kernel_entry`](/api/evoxc/external/get-external-kernel-entry/) — The `(callable, device_resident)` entry for `name` at `backend`.
- [`get_portable`](/api/evoxc/external/get-portable/) — The registered portable (`@evoxc.defn`) implementation for `name`.
- [`register_external_kernel`](/api/evoxc/external/register-external-kernel/) — Register `callable_` as the external kernel named `name`.
- [`register_portable`](/api/evoxc/external/register-portable/) — Register the optional graph decomposition for kernel `name`.
- [`unregister_external_kernel`](/api/evoxc/external/unregister-external-kernel/) — Remove every kernel slot AND the registered portable for `name`.
